title: Gate an NSX Policy group rename on a revision precheck
prompt:
Platform engineering needs a guarded NSX Policy group rename for VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1. Finish the `VcfNsxGroupGuard` PowerShell module so the current group is read and checked before the update. A failed precheck must be terminal: it must never issue the mutating request.

Before implementing, research the `ReadGroupForDomain` and `UpdateGroupForDomain` operations and their VMware VCF PowerCLI 9.1 generated bindings in official VMware sources. Confirm their parameters, request and response models, and optional-field behavior, and cite the source URLs consulted.

The supplied manifest must continue to require `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.SddcManager` version `13.5.0.25380678`; its official `VMware.OpenAPI` dependency loads the generated `VMware.Bindings.Nsx.Policy` client and model types used here. Do not install, copy, generate, or vendor any VMware module, assembly, binding, SDK, or OpenAPI specification. Production API traffic must use the supplied `VMware.Bindings.Nsx.Policy.Api.PolicyApi` instance. Do not bypass it with `Invoke-RestMethod`, `Invoke-WebRequest`, `HttpClient`, curl, raw sockets, or another direct REST client.

Export exactly one function:

`Set-VcfNsxGroupDisplayName -PolicyApi <VMware.Bindings.Nsx.Policy.Api.PolicyApi> -DomainId <string> -GroupId <string> -ExpectedRevision <int32> -ExpectedDisplayName <string> -DisplayName <string> [-Description <string>]`

- The `PolicyApi` is already configured and authenticated; its connection lifecycle remains caller-owned. Invoke `ReadGroupForDomain` exactly once. Reject a null response. The precheck passes only when the returned `Id` equals `GroupId`, its `Revision` equals `ExpectedRevision`, and its `DisplayName` equals `ExpectedDisplayName`. String comparisons are exact ordinal comparisons.
- If any precheck condition fails, throw a terminating error immediately. Do not construct a fallback result, retry, or call `UpdateGroupForDomain`.
- After a passing precheck, create a fresh real `VMware.Bindings.Nsx.Policy.Model.Group`. Set only `Revision` from the precheck response and `DisplayName` from the requested new value. Set `Description` only when the caller explicitly bound `-Description`. Leave `Id`, `ResourceType`, `Tags`, `Expression`, `Children`, and every other optional property unset.
- Invoke `UpdateGroupForDomain` exactly once with the same domain and group IDs plus that generated model. Reject a null update response and otherwise return the generated response object unchanged. Do not issue a second read or update.

Unset optional fields must be omitted from the JSON request, not sent as empty strings, empty arrays, false, zero, or null. In particular, an unbound `Description` must not appear in the PUT body.

Run `pwsh -NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File tests/verify.ps1`. Do not modify the module manifest; edit only `VcfNsxGroupGuard/VcfNsxGroupGuard.psm1`.
scenario: an NSX Policy group rename is permitted only when the just-read group identity, revision, and display name match the caller's precheck expectations
constraint: the protected verifier proves from the complete request log that a failed precheck issues no PUT and that a passing precheck sends only the intended Group members
